body:
`changed_paths` in `.github/workflows/tests.yml` carries
`if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'`. On a **push** to main it is skipped,
and every job gated on its `frontend` output skips with it — so **E2E Tests
(SPA) has never run on a main push**. Measured 2026-08-10 across the 12 most
recent main runs: `E2E Tests (SPA) | skipped | steps=0` on every one, including
`17c6ae1` (#1508), the commit that ADDED both the reader-notes feature and
`frontend/e2e/reader-notes.spec.ts`.

The PR-side skip is deliberate and good — the comment explains it as not
charging a `.po`-only PR half an hour for a suite that cannot tell it anything.
The **push-side** consequence looks unintended: nothing in that rationale is
about main.

**Why it matters, concretely.** E2E gates a PR at the moment that PR is tested,
and main moves afterwards. Two PRs can each be green in isolation and red in
combination; nothing re-checks. The breakage then lands on main invisibly and
surfaces later on whatever unrelated PR happens to run E2E next — where it reads
as *that* PR's fault. The author's correct move (A/B against main) does not clear
it either, because **main has no E2E result to compare against.**

Observed exactly this on #1533: E2E passed at head `c9a4b5a` (success, 21 steps)
and failed at `b2de7f8`, where the only difference was a findings JSON and a
Python unit test — no frontend code whatsoever. `reader-notes.spec.ts` was
present and passing at the earlier head. So the PR was the messenger.

Note the summary job reports `success` when a required job is `skipped`, which is
correct for a deliberate skip but means the dashboard cannot distinguish "E2E
passed" from "E2E never ran". Related: F-81d428 (a gate written as "nothing was
bad" admits every state that is neither good nor bad).

Options, cheapest first:
1. Run `changed_paths` on push too, diffing `github.event.before...github.sha`,
   so a frontend-touching merge re-runs E2E on main.
2. Run E2E unconditionally on main pushes (costs a full suite per merge).
3. A scheduled main-only E2E run — but this repo forbids new scheduled jobs, so
   an event-driven variant of (1) is the fit here.
title: the SPA e2e suite never runs on main, so a regression from two independently-green PRs is invisible until an unrelated PR trips it
